intro: My personal takes, unfiltered opinions on games, tech, movies, and whatever else is on my mind. These are mine, not anyone else's.

items.title: Returnal caps frame generation at 2X. The ceiling was one return value.
items.imageAlt: A dark Returnal forest with the headline 3X to 6X in a 2X game
body: Returnal was built against an NVIDIA SDK old enough that multi-frame generation did not exist yet, and the game hardcodes a request for exactly one generated frame. So 2X is its hard ceiling. I wrote a small proxy that translates the old SDK calls into the modern ones while the game runs, and the ceiling goes away: 3X, 4X, 5X and 6X, whichever you set.

The ceiling was not really in the game. It was in one inverted return value. The old SDK returns a boolean where true means success; the new one returns a code where zero means success. Passing that straight through turns every success into a failure, and the engine then never tags a single resource, so frame generation sits there fully configured and completely idle.

What it buys you is not a bigger number on the counter. At 2X the engine has to render 112 real frames to fill the display; at 4X it renders 56 for the same picture, and the GPU time that frees is what pays for neural rendering. With neural rendering on, 2X gives 130 fps and 4X gives 225. Fewer real frames, 73 percent more of them.
It is free, it is MIT licensed, and it works on Returnal and nothing else, deliberately.

items.title: OptiScaler and DLSS 5 in Returnal: the settings that actually work
body: A second run at DLSS 5 in Returnal, through a different implementation. The frame rate roughly doubled to about 133 fps at 4K, the game's own HDR started working correctly, and the driver-level HDR workaround the first write-up recommended is no longer needed.

Three of the controls do the opposite of what their names suggest. Colour strength moved the picture's colour by 20% while adding no detail at all. Intensity, despite being described as the overall strength, measured below the noise floor. And pushing a control past the interface's cap made it measurably worse on both counts, not better.

It also documents where the measurements failed. One setting scored +50% detail and turned out to be a repeating pattern invented on flat stone, with the character's suit crushed to black. Two purpose-built instruments could not see it. A person could, instantly.
items.imageAlt: OptiScaler and DLSS 5 settings in Returnal

items.title: DLSS 5 Neural Rendering in Returnal: measured, not eyeballed
body: DLSS 5 Neural Rendering can produce a dramatic before-and-after image. I tested it in Returnal at 4K to find out how much of the difference survives measurement, which controls genuinely matter, and what the effect costs in motion.

Switching it on increased measured edge detail by about 50% on the character crop and 29% on the environment crop. Natural at Intensity 1.0 was the important choice, while Local Structure 2.0 scored higher but made foliage visibly speckled.
The full write-up includes the floating-point method, the corrected performance figures, lower-generation GPU evidence, final settings, and every conclusion that changed after a second test.

items.title: Why I started writing my opinions here
body: This is where I'll drop my honest take on things: games, tech, movies, the internet, whatever's got my attention that week.
No corporate filter, no pretending to like something I don't. If you came for my opinion, this is the page. More coming soon.
